correctness.rationale: For a smooth n-circle link L and s punctures, Alexander duality in S^3 for L plus infinity plus punctures gives H^1=Z^n and H^2=Z^(n+s), no torsion or higher cohomology. Excision and the deleted-point long exact sequence split H^2 into the old complement classes and puncture summands; global pairwise Gauss maps restrict as an integral identity matrix on the small puncture spheres. These are a global fiberwise Z-basis in the Fadell–Neuwirth bundle, so integral Leray–Hirsch proves the product over all k by induction. Codimension-three general position gives pi_1(F_k(M))=pi_1(M)^k; the trefoil group surjects onto S3 while the unknot group is Z, proving non-homotopy equivalence. The statement makes no cup-product-ring claim.

originality.rationale: The 2026 primary source defines ordered link-complement fibers for trivial unlinks and studies fundamental groups, not integral additive cohomology. A particularly close earlier paper computes unordered configuration homology, including mod-two knot-complement tables, and does not provide the ordered integral product for all links and all particle counts. Direct implication checks show neither stronger source includes the asserted ordered integral all-link theorem; relevant search coverage is documented, with residual risk of unindexed classical literature.
residual_risks: An unindexed preexisting ordered-configuration-space theorem may already state this explicit all-link all-k integral factorization, despite no equivalent result in the inspected close sources.
The paper of Bödigheimer–Cohen–Taylor covers analogous knot-complement blindness for unordered mod-two groups; the asserted novelty is restricted to ordered integral all-k cohomology.
No claim about integral cup products or unordered configuration spaces follows from the additive calculation.

value.rationale: The newly defined ordered-point fibers of mixed link configurations motivate a complete additive integral invariant. The all-k formula for arbitrary linked or knotted embeddings and the rigorous knot-group counterexample demonstrate a structural inability of the entire integral Betti profile to detect ambient knotting, while explaining why stronger invariants remain necessary. This is not a finite data recomputation or arbitrary parameter slice.
